Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:1:1.hebrew: עידית וזיבורית נזקין בעידית ובעל חוב וכתובת אשה בזיבורית - מדאורייתא ב"ח בזיבורית, כדלקמן. ורבנן הוא דתקון ליה בבינונית משום נעילת דלת ללוין, והיכא דלית ליה בינונית ליתא לתקנתא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:1:1.english: Best-quality [land] and worst-quality [land] — damages are paid from the best-quality, while a creditor and a woman's marriage contract [are collected] from the worst-quality - By Torah law, a creditor collects from the worst-quality [land], as [stated] below. It was the Rabbis who enacted for him [collection] from medium-quality [land], so as not to lock the door before borrowers; and where he has no medium-quality [land], the enactment does not apply.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:2:1.english: Make his medium [field] like the best - For it is his best [property].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:3:1.english: And he sold it - After the loan, since the middling [land] had been bound to the creditor from the outset, while the choice land was still in his possession.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:7:1.hebrew: אידי ואידי שלא היתה לו עידית - ודכ"ע בשל עולם הן שמין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:7:1.english: Both this and that [refer to a case where] he had no *idit* [land] - And according to everyone, they assess [the damages] from the property of the world, [i.e., the average land of the general population].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:7:2.hebrew: ולא קשיא כו' - הא דקתני ב"ח וכתובת אשה בזיבורית, דשויא בינונית דידיה כעידית דעלמא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:7:2.english: And it is not difficult, etc. - That which it teaches that a creditor and a woman's marriage contract [are collected] from the poorest-quality land is [in a case] where his medium-quality [land] is equivalent to the best-quality land of other people.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:8:1.hebrew: אידי ואידי [כגון] שהיתה בינונית שלו כבינונית דעלמא - ולא היתה לו עידית מתחילה, ובהא פליגי: דתנא דמתניתא קמייתא סבר בשל עולם הן שמין, ואמטו להכי שקיל ב"ח בבינונית כדיניה, ואידך סבר בשלו הן שמין. ל"א גרסינן אידי ואידי כגון שהיתה בינונית שלו כעידית דעלמא, ומפרשינן ליה הכי: אידי ואידי כשהיתה לו עידית ומכרה, ובהא פליגי: דתנא דמתניתא קמייתא סבר בשלו הן שמין, וכיון דלדידיה הואי בינונית, אע"ג דלעלמא עידית, מיניה משלם; ותנא דברייתא סבר בשל עולם הן שמין. ותפוס לשון ראשון:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 8a:8:1.english: Both this and that [refer to a case where] his average-quality [land] was like the average-quality [land] of everyone else - and he did not originally have any best-quality land. And in this they disagree: the Tanna of the first Mishnah holds that they assess according to [the land of] people in general, and therefore the creditor collects from average-quality land as is his due; and the other holds that they assess according to his own [land]. Another explanation: We read, "Both this and that [refer to a case where] his average-quality [land] was like the best-quality land of everyone else," and we explain it thus: both this and that refer to a case where he had best-quality land and sold it. And in this they disagree: the Tanna of the first Mishnah holds that they assess according to his own [land], and since for him it was average-quality, even though for others it is best-quality, he pays from it; and the Tanna of the Baraita holds that they assess according to [the land of] people in general. And hold on to the first explanation.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 8a:7:1.hebrew: ה"ג אידי ואידי בשלא היתה לו עידית ומכרה, הא דשויא בינונית דידיה כעידית דעלמא, הא דלא שויא כו' - והא דקאמר: "אידי ואידי כגון שלא היתה לו עידית ומכרה", ולא בעי למימר דתרוייהו מיירי שלא היה לו כלל — דא"כ, ההוא דמיירי דשויא בינונית דידיה כעידית דעלמא, אמאי קרי לה בינונית? אלא ה"ק: אידי ואידי שלא היתה לו עידית ומכרה, כלומר: לא איירי כשהיתה לו עידית ומכרה, אלא בחדא מיירי שלא היתה לו מעולם, וחדא מיירי כשהיתה לו ועדיין יש לו; ואין צריך לאוקמי כשמכר שום שדה, וסברי תרוייהו בשל עולם הן שמין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 8a:7:1.english: Thus we read: "Both this and that are where it is not [a case where] he had idit and sold it; this one, where his medium [land] is worth like the idit of the world; that one, where it is not worth [that], etc." - And as for what [the Gemara] says, "both this and that are where it is not [a case where] he had idit and sold it" — it does not mean to say that both discuss a case where he never had [idit] at all, for if so, regarding the one that discusses [the case] where his medium [land] is worth like the idit of the world, why does it call it "medium"? Rather, this is what it means: both this and that are where it is not [a case where] he had idit and sold it; that is, it does not discuss [a case] where he had idit and sold it, but rather, one [case] discusses where he never had [idit], and the other discusses where he had [idit] and still has it. And there is no need to establish [the case] as one where he sold some field, and both [Tannaim] hold that they assess according to [the standard of] the world.
